title: When one goes up, does the other?
objectives: Tell direct from inverse proportion with the ratio test and the product test
Solve a problem with inverse proportion by keeping the product fixed
Recognise a link that is neither

screens.prose: 4 painters take 6 days to paint a house. Every painter works at the same speed, and more painters share the same job.
screens.question: Drag the point at 8 painters to the number of days the job takes.

hints.text: With twice as many painters, does the job take longer or shorter?
8 painters is double 4 painters.
Double the painters share the work, so each day gets twice as much done. The days halve.

feedback.correct: Twice the painters, half the days.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask how much painting gets done each day with 8 painters.

byKey.direct: You doubled the days along with the painters. More painters share the work, so the job gets shorter.
byKey.minus: You took 4 days off for 4 more painters. Doubling the team halves the time: 6 ÷ 2.
byKey.same: The team doubled, so the job cannot take as long as before.

explain.text: Doubling the painters halves the days, so 8 painters take 3 days. The job is a fixed 4 × 6 = 24 painter-days, and 8 × 3 = 24 too.

screens.prose: You have £1,200 to spend on one company's shares. The curve shows how many shares each price buys. Drag the point along the curve.
screens.question: At what share price does £1,200 buy exactly 40 shares?

hints.text: Watch the number of shares as you drag. Stop when it reads 40.
The curve passes 40 shares between £25 and £35.
40 shares at £30 each cost 40 × £30 = £1,200.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drag until the label reads 40 shares.

byKey.forty: You set the price to £40. At £40 each, £1,200 buys 30 shares, not 40.

explain.text: At £30 a share, 40 shares cost exactly £1,200. Every point on the curve has price × shares = 1,200. A higher price buys fewer shares.

screens.prose: Price × shares stayed at £1,200 along the whole curve. When the product of two amounts is fixed, they are in **inverse proportion**: double one, and the other halves.
screens.question: The price rises from £30 to £60. How many shares does £1,200 buy now?

hints.text: The price doubled. What happens to the number of shares?
Follow the curve to a price of £60.

feedback.correct: Double the price, half the shares.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep price × shares at £1,200.

byKey.direct: You doubled the shares with the price. Dearer shares mean fewer for the same money.
byKey.additive: You took 30 off the shares because the price rose by £30. Inverse proportion divides: 1,200 ÷ 60.

explain.text: The price doubled, so the number of shares halved, from 40 to 20. Check: 20 × £60 = £1,200. The product stays fixed while the two amounts move opposite ways.

screens.prose: Now the price does not double. It rises from £30 to £48, still with £1,200 to spend.
screens.question: How many shares does £1,200 buy at £48 each?

hints.text: The product of price and shares is still £1,200.
The dashed line meets the curve at the answer.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the fixed £1,200 by the new price.

byKey.direct: You scaled the shares up by 48/30 = 1.6. A higher price buys fewer shares, so divide by 1.6.
byKey.additive: You took 18 shares off for an £18 rise. The fixed product, not the gap, decides the answer.

explain.text: The price rose by a factor of 48 ÷ 30 = 1.6, so the shares fall by the same factor: 40 ÷ 1.6 = 25. Directly, £1,200 ÷ £48 = 25 shares.

screens.prose: No curve this time, only data. A batch of identical jobs runs on several identical machines. You decide which link the numbers follow.
screens.question: How many hours do 6 machines take?

hints.text: Multiply each pair. What do you notice?
Each row multiplies to the same number.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Test the product of each pair.

byKey.direct: You scaled 15 hours up by 3 for three times the machines. More machines finish sooner.
byKey.pattern: You continued the drops in the column, 5 then 4 then 3. The rule is in the products, not the gaps.
byKey.halve: You halved the 15 hours, but 15 hours belongs to 2 machines. Six machines is double 3 machines, so halve their 10 hours: 5.

explain.text: Every row multiplies to 30 machine-hours: 2 × 15, 3 × 10 and 5 × 6. That fixed product means inverse proportion. So 6 machines take 30 ÷ 6 = 5 hours.

screens.prose: A car starts with 40 litres of fuel and burns 5 litres an hour. As the hours rise, the fuel left falls.
screens.question: Is the fuel left in inverse proportion to the hours driven?

options.text: Yes: one goes up as the other goes down
options.why: Moving in opposite directions is not enough. After 2 hours 30 litres are left; after 4 hours, 20 litres, not 15.

options.text: No: hours × fuel left is not fixed

options.why: Direct proportion is a line through (0, 0) that rises. This line starts at 40 litres and falls.

hints.text: Test it: if the hours double, does the fuel left halve?
Read the fuel left at 2 hours and at 4 hours.
2 × 30 = 60, but 4 × 20 = 80. The product changes.

feedback.correct: The product changes, so it is not inverse proportion.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply hours by fuel left at two points and compare.

byKey.opposite: You took opposite movement as the test. Inverse proportion needs a fixed product, and 2 × 30 is not 4 × 20.

explain.text: Check the product: 2 × 30 = 60, but 4 × 20 = 80. It is not fixed, so this is not inverse proportion. The fuel drops by the same 5 litres each hour: a falling straight line.

screens.prose: Two tests sort every pair of amounts. $$\text{direct: } \frac{y}{x} = k, \text{ so } y = kx \qquad \text{inverse: } xy = c, \text{ so } y = \frac{c}{x}$$ Direct is a straight line through the origin. Inverse is a curve that never meets an axis.
screens.question: A trip of 120 miles is driven at different steady speeds. How is the journey time linked to the speed?

options.why: At 40 mph the trip takes 3 hours; at 60 mph, 2 hours. The ratios 3/40 and 2/60 differ.
Check the product: 40 × 3 = 60 × 2 = 120. It is fixed.

feedback.correct: Distance = speed × time, and the distance is fixed.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Try two speeds and test the product.

explain.text: Speed × time is the distance, fixed at 120 miles. A fixed product is inverse proportion, so time $= \tfrac{120}{\text{speed}}$. Doubling the speed halves the time.

screens.prose: Solve an inverse problem without a graph. 4 painters take 6 days. How long do 3 painters take?
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: Total work: $4 \times 6 = 24$ painter-days, the fixed product
For 3 painters: $3 \times d = 24$, since the product stays fixed
Check: fewer painters take more days, as inverse proportion needs

hints.text: What stays the same whatever the team size?
The fixed product comes from the pair you know.
Find the product, write the equation, solve it, then check the direction.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the fixed product first.

byKey.new: The equation needs the 24 painter-days, so that line comes first.
byKey.solve: You can only divide once you have the equation $3d = 24$.

explain.text: You found the fixed work, 24 painter-days, and kept it for the new team. Then $3d = 24$ gives $d = 8$. Three painters take longer than four, which matches the direction.

screens.prose: A fund puts the same £10,000 into each stock it buys. Stock A trades at £25.00, so the fund buys 400 shares. Stock B trades at £62.50.
screens.question: How many shares of B does the fund buy?

hints.text: Is the number of shares directly or inversely linked to the price?
Price × shares is fixed at £10,000.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The money per stock is fixed, so divide it by the price.

byKey.direct: You scaled the shares up with the price. A dearer stock gets fewer shares for the same £10,000.
byKey.additive: You took off the £37.50 price gap. The fixed amount is the money, so divide £10,000 by £62.50.

explain.text: Each position costs £10,000, so price × shares is fixed. B's price is 2.5 times A's, so the fund buys 400 ÷ 2.5 = 160 shares. Check: 160 × £62.50 = £10,000.

ideas: In direct proportion the ratio $y/x$ is fixed: double one, double the other.
In inverse proportion the product $xy$ is fixed: double one, halve the other.
Moving in opposite directions is not enough. Test the product before you call it inverse.

formula.name: Inverse proportion
formula.note: Find $c$ from one known pair, then divide.

summary.trap: A falling line is not inverse proportion. Check that the product stays the same.

quiz.prose: Four situations, each pairing two amounts.
quiz.question: Which pair is in inverse proportion?

options.text: The number of equal partners, and each partner's slice of a £90,000 profit
The number of shares bought at £4.20 each, and the total cost
options.why: The cost is 4.20 × shares: a fixed ratio, so that is direct proportion.

options.text: Gym visits in a month, and a bill of £20.00 plus £5.00 a visit
options.why: The fixed £20.00 breaks both tests. Doubling the visits neither doubles nor halves the bill.

options.text: Hours since a 40-litre tank was filled, and the fuel left at 5 litres an hour
options.why: Falling is not enough. Hours × fuel left changes, from 1 × 35 = 35 to 2 × 30 = 60.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look for the pair whose product stays fixed.

explain.text: Partners × slice is the whole £90,000, a fixed product. Twice the partners gives each half the slice. That is inverse proportion.

quiz.prose: 6 servers process a batch of data in 10 minutes. Every server works at the same rate.
quiz.question: How many minutes do 15 servers take?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the fixed product first.

byKey.direct: You scaled the time up with the servers. More servers finish sooner.
byKey.additive: You took 9 minutes off for 9 more servers. The product, 60 server-minutes, is what stays fixed.

explain.text: The batch is 6 × 10 = 60 server-minutes of work. With 15 servers it takes 60 ÷ 15 = 4 minutes.

quiz.prose: $y$ is directly proportional to $x$, and $y = 18$ when $x = 4$.
quiz.question: Find $y$ when $x = 10$.

byKey.additive: You added 6 to both. Direct proportion multiplies: x grew 2.5 times, so y does too.
byKey.inverse: You kept the product fixed. That is inverse proportion; here the ratio is fixed.

quiz.prose: $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$, and $y = 18$ when $x = 4$.
quiz.question: Find $y$ when $x = 6$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the fixed product $xy$ first.

byKey.direct: You scaled y up with x. Inverse proportion divides: x grew 1.5 times, so y shrinks 1.5 times.
byKey.additive: You took 2 off y because x rose by 2. The product xy, not the gap, stays fixed.
